review_notes: I read the whole file. Its definitions are dyadicCut, dyadicBump, dyadicFactor, DyadicBand, dyadicMultiFactor and dyadicBox. dyadicCut is built directly on Real.smoothTransition, and the rest are concrete constructions on top of it: a specific dyadic annular partition of unity, a product over an index type, and a Fintype.piFinset box. A grep of Mathlib turned up only Dyadic number-type definitions, which are unrelated to this concept. I found no Mathlib declaration for a dyadic-shell smooth partition of unity. Mathlib's general partition-of-unity API is a different, more abstract concept. The file reuses Real.smoothTransition, Fintype.piFinset and Finset.sum_prod_piFinset, so it does not compete with them. DyadicBand is a small named predicate with no clear Mathlib equivalent. The same repo has many other cutoff files, but the rubric concerns concepts already in Mathlib and I found no case for consolidation. I did not compare those files in detail, and any overlap among them is out of scope here.
